# Hands (browser and Mac control) (area `hands`)

Acting on the Mac and in browsers in the background: the extension, its protocol and store listing, native host, Mac input, downloads, tab groups.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **HAND-1** (agent): A frame whose address is a known challenge frame (Cloudflare Turnstile, hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA, Arkose, DataDome, AWS WAF, GeeTest; snapshot.CHALLENGE_FRAMES) puts `bot_check` {widgets, frames, ability browser_verification, read} first in the snapshot result.
- **HAND-2** (agent): browsing.owner_profile ("browser/folder", the owner's pick in the app) is used by the browser resolver for an owner task with no profile named only while FERB has no profile of its own and that profile is paired. With FERB's own profile configured nothing changes: it stays the default.
- **HAND-200** (owner): In-app shortcuts go through unchanged. cmd+q and cmd+h go through FERB's safe quit/hide, which acts only on apps FERB launched and checks for unsaved work. Screen-wide combos (cmd+tab, cmd+space, ctrl+arrows, force quit) are refused.
- **HAND-201** (owner): One collapsed, labelled group per task with only FERB's tabs. FERB never closes a tab it didn't open; a borrowed owner tab is never grouped or closed. A result tab is handed over (moved out, open); the rest close at task end. A tab dragged out becomes the owner's; one dragged in stays the owner's. Closing a FERB tab or the group mid-task = owner stopping that part (FERB asks to continue). "Keep the tabs open" ungroups them; pause keeps the group; loops keep it collapsed; after a reconnect or restart FERB re-adopts or closes it (no orphans).
- **HAND-203** (owner): Terminal commands can't write, truncate, delete or rename in the owner's visible folders (non-hidden folders in home, iCloud Drive, /Volumes) unless the folder is named, in the owner's words or in the plan line FERB stated and the owner didn't correct. Hidden folders, ~/Library (minus the protection lists), temp folders and FERB's workspace stay writable. Kernel-enforced by the sandbox after shell expansion. The owner's files change through file tools (backup copies); a refused command tells the worker why.
- **HAND-204** (owner): Code never fuzzy-matches folder names. The planner resolves what the owner meant (typos included) into a structured `folders` task field, shown in the plan line ("I'll work in ~/Downloads"); code allows exactly those paths. An ambiguous name gets one which-question. Work starts at once; a wrong guess the owner doesn't correct is covered by snapshots and file-tool backups.
- **HAND-205** (owner): Any path with a component starting with "." (e.g. ~/Desktop/repo/.git) counts as a program folder and stays writable, so git works in any repo; snapshots cover mistakes.
- **HAND-206** (owner): A fresh APFS local snapshot is taken before each terminal command, skipped only if no command ran since the last one. FERB says so when a snapshot couldn't be taken (e.g. a nearly full disk). Snapshots last about 24 hours and don't cover external drives.
- **HAND-207** (owner): FERB's own tabs are muted by default unless the task needs to listen. FERB stopping or changing playback in a tab the owner is using counts as a disturbance fact. A general "keep a tab playing while the owner switches away" ability comes later.
- **HAND-208** (owner): Workers use the browser_verification ability for a visible "verify you are human" check; browser_handoff is the fallback. Code states the fact and names the ability; no extra prompt wording about what counts as a bypass.
- **HAND-210** (owner): No per-file size cap and no question (a download isn't hard to undo). Per task: 300 files and 32 GB. The 10 GB free-disk floor stays. Shell downloads (curl, brew, pip, git clone, huggingface-cli, docker pull) count against the same per-task budget and floor; a command that would break either is stopped and the worker is told plainly why (a fact, not a judgment). Unchanged: the downloads folder keeps to 20 GB (over-cap handling: HAND-211), 50 tabs per task, no time-based clearing, a browser download never opens a Save dialog.
- **HAND-211** (owner): When ~/.ferb/workspace/downloads goes over its 20 GB cap, FERB asks, showing how much would go and how many files (oldest first, enough to get back under). Yes deletes them permanently; No or no answer does nothing, and FERB doesn't ask again until the folder grows past the cap by a further meaningful amount. The question uses the existing owner-question path, isn't tied to a task, and is rule 5's permanent-deletion confirmation. Only files inside that folder go, never through a link; each deletion is journaled with counts and bytes, never names.
- **HAND-212** (owner): When an app brings itself to the front in answer to FERB's background action, FERB doesn't put the owner's app back and doesn't ask. The worker is told as a fact and the trace shows it. FERB prefers routes that open no window (mdfind, AX reads, read-only AppleScript, a quiet reopen); lessons reach how-notes and playbooks. Code never scans AppleScript for "activate": the after-call fact covers it.
- **HAND-213** (owner): A tab sound change is not recorded when Chrome says the owner muted or unmuted it (mutedInfo.reason == "user") or when the owner's own keyboard or mouse input was under way at that moment. Only changes FERB could have caused are recorded: a structural fact, not a judgment.
- **HAND-214** (agent): A command connects directly only to FERB-sandboxed listeners that existed when it started (plus pinned ports); anything later goes through the egress proxy, which checks contained listeners too (NO_PROXY empty).
- **HAND-215** (agent): Visible folders (HAND-203) include non-hidden files directly in ~ and tool folders like ~/go. A task that needs one names it in the plan line; snapshots cover mistakes.
- **HAND-216** (agent): After a failed snapshot the next attempt waits 60 s (RETRY_AFTER_FAILURE_S); each result in between still states that no snapshot was taken.
- **HAND-217** (agent): `shell.send` into a command started with a lift is refused. The shell profile has `(deny signal)(allow signal (target same-sandbox))`: a command signals its own children and setsid descendants, never other programs or other FERB commands (so it can't kill the daemon or the proxy).
- **HAND-218** (agent): Into a focused password field, a key press is refused only when it enters text: a character key without cmd/ctrl, Space, or a paste (cmd+V by key or the Paste menu item). Return, Tab, Escape, arrows and other shortcuts still go. The browser applies the same rule (content.js, background.js, ext_bridge).
- **HAND-219** (agent): Refused as screen-wide besides HAND-200's list: opt+cmd+H (hide others), ctrl+Space, ctrl+cmd+Q (lock), shift+cmd+Q (log out). cmd+M stays in-app. The guard also covers a menu item whose key equivalent is cmd+Q/cmd+H (mac.menu, a press or click on the item).
- **HAND-220** (agent): mac.act: the snapshot window's window-server id + the element's AX role path, role, subrole, label (sibling index only when unlabelled), never the snapshot id or the value. mac.click/mac.pointer: the shot's window id + the element under the point; with no element or one larger than 400 pt, the point on a 24 pt grid of the window. Window titles are left out. A collision only asks the owner.
- **HAND-221** (agent): AX messaging timeout 2 s (macOS default 6 s), set globally and on each app element. A walk stops after 8 s or 60,000 elements, marked `budget`; it then can't tell about password fields and captures fall back to text recognition.
- **HAND-222** (agent): welcome and cmd are {type, seq, body, mac}, HMAC-SHA256(pairing key, nonce|seq|type|body) with the hello's fresh nonce and a per-connection counter; each part of an assembled command and the envelope are verified. Unsigned replies change no page. A command that fails verification is dropped without a reply, so the daemon times out (unknown, the safe side). The extension accepts `paired` only during pairing.
- **HAND-223** (agent): The daemon takes a native-host connection only when the host's parent process runs a browser app FERB knows (peer_refusal, the .app's bundle id via libproc), and a paired profile's hello only from that browser. Any process of the owner's user can still start a browser binary with its own profile or read a pairing key from extension storage: same-uid processes are trusted.
- **HAND-224** (agent): For reads (list_tabs, snapshot, wait, screenshot(_part), record_frame, frame_origin, read_source, window_secrets, find, result_part, ping, point, dialog without a decision) an error, timeout or dropped connection is a DriverError, never OutcomeUnknown.
- **HAND-225** (agent): A browser act's identity is the page origin+path (and a child frame's), role, and the backend node id, else the DOM path when the accessibility pass gave none. A re-render that replaces the node escapes the identity; a shifted DOM path can collide (only asks the owner).
- **HAND-226** (agent): Sockets are read with libproc in FERB's own process (no subprocess; an answer of any size other than 792 bytes is no reading). The proxy route uses only it: the connected server socket must belong to an inspectable process. The profile route's direct ports need every user's listeners: nettop adds the uninspectable ones (unnamed, never pinned), counted only when it lists every listener libproc found and every line parses. Shared sockets are checked once per process.
- **HAND-227** (agent): LocalAccess.connected re-reads while a visible listener on that port has a queued connection, at most ACCEPT_WAIT = 30 s (the proxy's own connect timeout), then refuses; with nothing queued on a visible listener it refuses at once.
- **HAND-228** (agent): The shell's egress proxy and the Claude runtime's tool-list relay listen with socket.SOMAXCONN (capped by kern.ipc.somaxconn, 128 here), not socketserver's default 5.
- **HAND-229** (agent): Muting is chrome.tabs.update({muted}), never the page's media. A tab FERB opens (and a popup a FERB tab opens) is muted before anything loads. The owner's tabs are never muted or unmuted (`mute_tab` refuses them). audio.listen, browser.record with_audio or the worker's browser_media unmute unmutes that FERB tab for the rest of the task. A tab that becomes the owner's gets its sound back only when FERB's extension muted it. Results carry `tab_muted`, never failing the call.
- **HAND-230** (agent): A sound change in a tab that isn't FERB's is recorded for each active task with an acting call in flight or ended within SOUND_NEAR_S = 5 s, and not when the owner's input is under way or ended within OWNER_NEAR_S = 3 s. Attribution stays temporal correlation only; no URL or title is kept.
- **HAND-231** (agent): Downloads owns one byte budget per task tree: files the tree's tabs took + transfers arriving + bytes its shell commands received through the egress proxy (shell_downloads, survives a restart). Only received bytes count. The 300-file count is the browser's only: the proxy sees connections, not files; the byte budget and the floor cover the shell.
- **HAND-232** (agent): While any FERB command runs, every WATCH_S = 1 s the bytes each command received go to the daemon; past the tree's budget or under the free-disk floor (or free space unreadable) that command's group is stopped with `stopped_by_ferb` and `shell.download_stopped` journaled. Only a command that received bytes in that second is stopped: unzipping or building isn't a download.
- **HAND-233** (agent): A transfer fails only when no byte arrives for STALL_S = 60 s; a slow download that keeps moving is never cut. Parts are 512 KiB, sent whole (never split into result parts).
- **HAND-234** (agent): browser.task_max_tabs (50) counts the still-open tabs FERB opened for the task tree in every driver (worker's, a link's, a page's popup, tabs opened from a borrowed tab) plus opens in flight; never the borrowed tab, a handed-over tab or a closed one. Past it: the open is refused, a link isn't handed to the browser, a popup is closed while blank (popup_refused).
- **HAND-235** (agent): A page's saves past the hold caps (20 per tab, 100 in all) are dropped (never the browser's), and every drop is reported: the first of a document at once, then those within the minute in one event with `count`.
- **HAND-236** (agent): browser.download_task_max_gb (32), download_total_gb (20), download_min_free_gb (10), in decimal GB as the owner and Finder count. A one-time journaled upgrade (download-limits-2026-10-31) removes the MB keys; an owner's own MB value carries over converted; a removed key is never read.
- **HAND-237** (agent): browser_downloads tells the worker to move the file (mv, not cp) where the owner asked, else ~/Downloads, and name that path. HAND-203's scope still applies to the destination.
- **HAND-238** (agent): No pre-activation refusal because a FERB app is in front (right after a Yes in the notch FERB is in front). Input stays out of FERB's own apps by: waiting for the owner to be quiet, activating the target, posting each event only while the target is front (PointerInterrupted otherwise); `_own_point` refusing a real click/scroll a FERB window would take, before and right before each event; every Mac tool refusing to target FERB's apps.
- **HAND-239** (agent): apps.launch uses `open -g -b` (not -j). An app the owner hid is not unhidden.
- **HAND-240** (agent): mac.open takes a path or an http/https url and opens it with NSWorkspace, activates = false. The file goes through the protection lists as a read; a url is an OPEN_TAB to its site (address checks apply). A path Launch Services counts an application is refused; installed apps open by bundle_id. A windowless running app gets the reopen Apple Event without kAECanSwitchLayer, only when it shows no window.
- **HAND-241** (agent): A file whose Launch Services type conforms to executable, script, installer package, configuration profile, shortcut/workflow, or is a package directory (unknown or unreadable type counts) goes through the terminal question with path, hash and text; the Yes covers those bytes, re-hashed before the open. It applies to mac.open and to every open by default app via FERB's input. Skipped when the receiving app declares itself the file's Editor (CFBundleDocumentTypes role); a configuration profile always asks; a file a script names keeps the type-only rule.
- **HAND-242** (agent): After a No, or while the question waits, the downloads-cap question (HAND-211) is asked again only once the folder is a further 10% of the cap (2 GB of 20 GB) past the size it was asked at; the newer question replaces the waiting one. After a Yes the next pass over the cap asks afresh. Yes deletes only regular files the question counted, through the open folder (O_NOFOLLOW).
- **HAND-243** (agent): The shell profile denies mach-lookup of com.apple.windowserver.active and com.apple.windowserver, so no command can post input events or capture the screen around the always-ask rules. Full Disk Access is kept for the shell; mac.applescript's profile is unchanged.
- **HAND-244** (agent): HAND-203 is enforced with `deny file-write*` on visible folders and a later `allow file-write*` regex for any path component starting with "." (last match wins).
- **HAND-245** (owner): The shell can reach any site; every connection is recorded in the trace. Sending private data from the browser still asks (the sink rule). The browser URL sink therefore guards only browser navigation (accepted residual).
- **HAND-246** (agent): The download floor (browser.download_min_free_gb, 10 GB) and the shell download watch read the volume's available capacity for important usage (NSURLVolumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey: free plus purgeable space), falling back to statvfs free space when macOS doesn't give it. The number itself is unchanged.
- **HAND-247** (agent): One table (autoinstall.INSTALL, a row per profiles.BROWSERS entry) says how FERB reaches each browser: the documented install request, the request written but unconfirmed (Brave, Edge), or none (Arc, Vivaldi, Opera). Each adds FERB from its Chrome Web Store page (Add to <browser>); Load unpacked is offered only while no store id is set. A browser's executable is found by bundle id through Launch Services, /Applications/<app>.app when it knows none.
- **HAND-300** (agent): The bot_check fact states plainly that a bot-check widget's frame is on the page and that it may be only a passive badge that blocks nothing; the page's own words say whether a check is asked. No prompt or fact wording about bypasses.
- **HAND-400** (owner): FERB does not recognise music by its sound. Workers keep being told so: asked what a song is, they listen on the tab the owner means and, hearing no lyrics they can identify, say so, never naming something else as the song.
- **HAND-401** (owner): While FERB listens to an app or tab, the owner hears it too: FERB captures the app's audio unmuted (a tab listen hears the whole browser).
- **HAND-402** (agent): Each Mac and browser capability declares what its call targets (`preview_target(args, owner, observed)` → `PreviewTarget`, beside `Point` in ferb/act/point.py); the gateway's hook asks the capability and checks no tool names. The declaration does no lookup: the target resolves at the first frame request, and the hook never raises, so a preview problem can't lose a successful call.
- **HAND-403** (owner): Every browser tool shares one check: a connected profile is used; one that isn't connected is started quietly with no window; if the extension still doesn't come, the profile's own window opens once (the accepted focus shift) and FERB carries on through the extension. A profile with no FERB window takes a background tab in one of its own windows; nothing asks the owner first unless the extension isn't paired.
- **HAND-404** (owner): extensions/store/listing.md is kept and refreshed before each extension upload.
- **HAND-405** (agent): A window capture that fails with ScreenCaptureKit's "Failed to start stream" is tried once more before it is reported as failed.
- **HAND-406** (agent): Every native-host connection or extension message FERB doesn't take is journaled browser.connection_refused with a reason code, its plain why and the profile or app when known (never contents), bounded by _Repeats. The version of every authenticated hello is kept in the pairing record, so after a restart a profile whose recorded version is below MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION is still named too old (update it) in the planner's facts, the browser tool's error, browser_profiles, browsers.list and setup.browsers. The minimum is unchanged.
- **HAND-407** (agent): The browser resolver, the drivers' wake and browser_profiles take the discovered profiles plus each paired (browser, folder) of a browser discovery returned no profile for (Full Disk Access off, its Local State unreadable), named by its folder (profiles.with_paired). A browser whose profiles were read keeps only those: a paired folder missing there is never started (that would create it). While the Full Disk Access gate is closed, a name the resolver can't find and browser_profiles say that FERB can't read profile names without Full Disk Access.
- **HAND-408** (agent): A tmutil snapshot name of the strict form com.apple.TimeMachine.YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS.local (composed by local_snapshot from tmutil's date digits alone) is stored in its recovery record as is; anything else tmutil said is redacted as before. The result also gives its date as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", which no redaction pass mistakes for a card. The redactor itself is unchanged.
- **HAND-409** (agent): When foreground input isn't available, RealInput and the Mac driver say why: "FERB is paused" only while sensing is paused; otherwise that FERB can't tell whether the owner is using the Mac because its owner-input watcher isn't running, and that the owner allows Input Monitoring for FERB. The daemon supplies the reason (desktop.py).
- **HAND-410** (agent): helper.request turns a failure into a message with what is known: the Keychain's OSStatus and Security's text when the helper reports them; with the pinned helper, which doesn't, a failed lookup runs the helper's present check (no value read) and says whether the Keychain didn't show the item (not saved, or keychain locked) or has it but didn't hand it over. Each failure is journaled secret.helper_failed (operation, service, status / message / found). Never the request, the value or the Keychain account. A sealed fill's error carries the reason.
- **HAND-411** (agent): Pair all still pairs only owner profiles whose FERB extension is on, on the owner's click, opening or restarting no browser. Its reply counts the owner's profiles and lists each other one in `skipped` with a reason and the owner's step, from facts already read (read_states, hub.problem): requested, not_added, off, removed, problem (HAND-406's words); journaled browsers.pair_all_skipped. FERB.app's one message (SetupModel.pairAllMessage, tour and Settings) is nil only when every owner profile is paired: else one line per profile, and none found says so.
- **HAND-412** (agent): setup.browsers_pairing streams Pair all (a plan, a result per profile as it lands, then the reply); FERB.app shows it live. From each profile's files FERB reads the copy's version and Chromium's disable reasons: below MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION it is skipped as too_old with no pairing page; off for new permissions says so. A pairing ends early when the hello was refused or the files now say off, gone or too old, and an unanswered page names the likely reason and the step. Owner's click only; minimum unchanged; no extra browser opens.
- **HAND-413** (agent): A profile Pair all skips as removed, not added or waiting for a restart (`can_add`) offers Add to <browser> in the tour's result and Settings → Browsers: on the owner's click FERB's store page opens in that profile, FERB reads the browsers every 1.5 s with a live line and Stop waiting, and once FERB is on there offers Pair (the owner's click). Waiting for a restart says so, with the store page as the faster way. No policy files; FERB restarts or quits no browser.
- **HAND-414** (owner): A browser is offered, discovered, paired, listed or asked about only while its app is actually installed on this Mac (its bundle id resolved through Launch Services), and its profiles come only from that browser's own Local State. A user-data folder an uninstalled browser left behind is ignored everywhere: setup.browsers, Pair all, the planner's facts, browser_profiles, the resolver, native-host manifest and Web Store request writes. profiles.BROWSERS stays only as the map of known browsers' data folders.
- **HAND-415** (agent): Setup also asks Launch Services which apps open https links. Each one whose Info.plist declares Chromium's extension file type (org.chromium.extension, kept from Chromium's app Info.plist; Electron apps don't declare it) and whose bundle id profiles.BROWSERS doesn't know is named in setup.browsers (`unsupported`), in `ferb setup`'s text and after Pair all in the tour and Settings → Browsers as "<App> isn't supported by FERB yet". A copy in a Trash is skipped; no list (Launch Services unavailable) names none.
- **HAND-416** (agent): A FERB entry in a profile's extensions.settings counts as installed only with an integer `location` and a non-empty string `path`, as Chromium's ExtensionPrefs::GetInstalledInfoHelper requires, and not with the old `state` 2 (an external extension the owner uninstalled). Keys left under the id otherwise read as not added. A store copy listed in `extensions.external_uninstalls`, or left with `state` 2, reads as removed, so Pair all offers Add to <browser> (HAND-413) and opens no pairing page there.
- **HAND-418** (agent): When the extension lets go of a tab (release_tab, close, a tab moved out of its group), it awaits only what the browser itself does: handing back or failing held responses (Fetch), the debugger's detach, the tab's removal. What only the page can answer (content.js's held saves, its disarm, the hook's removal, focus emulation off) is asked without waiting: detaching ends the session's hook and emulation anyway. So a frozen, discarded or loading page can't keep `release_tab` past its timeout. Extension 0.19.1; minimum stays 0.19.0.
- **HAND-419** (agent): One helper (leftover_lines) writes the answer's line for whatever a task's cleanup couldn't release: a tab by browser, profile and its last title (redacted): FERB's own "I couldn't close one tab I opened: … Close it if it's still open.", the owner's borrowed one still open as they left it (press Cancel if the browser says FERB is debugging it); terminal commands, apps, listening, recordings and a cleanup cut short each a short plain line. No raw error or tab id reaches the owner; the task.cleanup span keeps them.
- **HAND-421** (owner): FERB's extension doesn't request Chrome's history permission. Browsing history from before FERB's own record (the browser_tabs trail since install) stays out of background reach; reading a browser's own History page needs foreground use, which asks the owner as always. Adding the permission later is a new owner decision.
- **HAND-422** (agent): In the extension, an error raised while an acting command's tab is prepared for input (attach: the debugger, its frame sessions, focus emulation, FERB's viewport, the readiness probe), while it reads where the target is (topPoint; a scroll's container), or for an unknown op, is marked nothingSent: the outcome is "failed". From the command's first input event on (a move, a press, text, a page-script action, a file set) an error, timeout or detach stays "unknown". Extension 0.19.2; minimum stays 0.19.0.
- **HAND-423** (agent): The extension keeps a frame session's setup error by its session id: it goes when Chrome reports the frame session detached, isn't recorded when the frame went before its setup ended, and every new debugger session starts with no frame sessions and no errors. When attach finds an error of a frame session that is still there, it lets the debugger go and attaches once more (every frame set up afresh), unless the tab holds a download for FERB (letting go would hand it to the browser); if an error remains after that, the command fails with nothing sent (HAND-422).
- **HAND-424** (owner): Wherever FERB shows a browser profile (tour and playground, Settings → Browsers, pairing lines, owner-profile picker, identity step, About, the pair question, a leftover tab's line, the AI's facts and tool results), the account it is signed in to its browser with (Local State `user_name`) shows beside its name: only that account, nothing after the name when it isn't signed in, no badge. Read fresh each time, never stored or journaled by FERB. Without Full Disk Access none shows (HAND-407). No prompt rule makes FERB's own sentences repeat emails.
- **HAND-425** (owner): Refines HAND-204's wording: code's folder line under the plan line reads "Working in ~/Desktop." (the same list, the home folder shown as ~), not "I'll work in …". It shows only when the task has folders. Saved history keeps the text it was saved with.
- **HAND-426** (agent): For APP-777/778. One daemon function (_browsing) decides from config and pairing facts; every route (task, plan step, scheduled or restored run) applies it in run_tree before any worker: the worker, its steps' conversations and the task row become the owner's, so the owner's browser tools and checks apply unchanged. The question is FERB's own check outside any task (memory_questions, kind browsing): option words only, applied once by whichever path sees the answer; a restart drops it and the next need asks.
- **HAND-427** (owner): Extension 0.19.3 adds `pdf` and `pdf_part`: Chrome prints the tab (Page.printToPDF, exactly printBackground, preferCSSPageSize and landscape), as a read, split into parts like a screenshot. Nothing paints over a PDF, so a page with a password, code or card field anywhere, or whose fields can't be found, is withheld. Protocol stays 21 so every installed FERB keeps working. The owner publishes it; then the app adds the PDF tool and raises the minimum.
